sections.h2: Which floor of the Jackson County Courthouse is the Recorder on?
sections.html:
The third. The Jackson County Recorder works in the courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640, phone (740) 286-1919, fax (740) 286-8835. The county's Recorder page posts weekday hours of 8:30 am to 4:00 pm and a closure from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm for lunch, so arrive before 11:30 or after 12:30.

Cash, check and debit or credit cards are accepted, with a $2.00 service fee on cards. The county's official records begin in 1997. Anything older must be viewed and printed at the office, while later records are searchable online after you set up an account.

sections.h2: What are the Jackson County Recorder's listed prices?
sections.html:
A deed, mortgage, lease, affidavit or most other recordable paper costs $39.00 for its first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, with every printed side counted as a page. The fee page explains that Ohio sets these prices and that half funds the basic recording fee while half goes to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

ItemFee
Deed, mortgage or lease, first two pages$39.00
Each added page$8.00
Marginal notation (release, assignment, amendment)$4.00 each
Plat or condominium drawing, per 8 by 14 sheet$40.00
UCC financing statement tied to real estate$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Copy$2.00 per page
Certified copy$2.00 per page plus $1.00 for the seal

Source: Jackson County Recorder fee page. A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and a zoning resolution costs $50.00.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County Auditor add before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate transfers page prints a $4.00 per thousand conveyance fee and a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee. Its history note says the conveyance fee jumped from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price on March 24, 1993.

The Auditor is in the same courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, phone (740) 286-4231, open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. The Tools menu of the Auditor's website holds a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page. State law lays the fee on the grantor (R.C. 319.202(D)). The posted forms are:

  • DTE 100, the statement of value and fee receipt
  • DTE 100EX, the reason an exemption applies
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX for manufactured or mobile homes

The order is Auditor, then Recorder. According to the Recorder's site, changing the names on title means a new deed, which goes to the Auditor for transfer and then to recording.

sections.h2: What goes wrong if a Jackson County deed is never recorded?
sections.html:
A later buyer who did not know about it can win. R.C. 5301.25 says deeds must be recorded where the land lies, and until they are, they are treated as fraudulent against a subsequent purchaser in good faith.

The Recorder's site answers a few questions that come up before a sale:

  • Most records are public. Military service records go only to the veteran, with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, which the site prices at $46.00.
  • The office suggests an attorney or other professional to prepare deeds and similar papers.

A name error means a fresh deed, which repeats the Auditor and Recorder steps.

sections.h2: How do I order copies or search Jackson County records?
sections.html:
The county's Recorder page tells users to create an account to view most records online. Since official records begin in 1997, a deed from the 1980s means a trip to the courthouse.

To order an image, email the book and page of the document to recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. Each page costs $2.00, payable by cash or check. Anyone planning a listing can also open the Auditor's Sales Reports page, which sits beside the Conveyance Calculator and a Tax Estimator.

sections.h2: Which other papers does the Jackson County Recorder file, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
The fee page reaches well past deeds. These listed items turn up when a title search finds old liens or a prior owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or durable power of attorney for health care: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • personal property tax liens, workers' compensation liens, certificates of premium due, recognizance liens and unemployment compensation liens: no fee

The county ties each charge to R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. When a title search turns up an old lien, ask the Recorder which release applies and what it costs, since a release is a separate recording from the deed.

sections.h2: Can a new owner contest a Jackson County valuation after buying?
sections.html:
Yes, through the county Board of Revision. The Auditor's complaint page says the board has three members, the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners or their designees, and that it adjusts values, not tax dollars. A complaint is filed on form DTE 1 with the Auditor, who acts as the board's secretary, and the Auditor's public notice gives March 31 as the filing deadline.

The page adds several cautions. The form must show the owner's opinion of value on line 8 and be notarized. Ohio allows one filing per three-year period in general, and a withdrawn complaint still counts. The owner carries the burden of proof, and the board may raise the value, lower it or leave it alone. It will not consider a percentage jump in the tax bill or a neighbor's lower valuation.

For payment questions, the Auditor's site sends people to the County Treasurer at 740-286-2402. Real estate taxes can be paid online or by the Autoagent phone line, 1-844-674-1100.

sections.h2: What is Jackson County like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Jackson County was founded on March 1, 1818 and takes its name from Andrew Jackson. Wikipedia calls it the Little Wales of Ohio. Its past runs through the Hanging Rock Iron Region: the Jefferson Iron Furnace went up in 1854, county iron went into the USS Monitor, and coal and salt mining followed. Furnace remnants stand in Jackson Lake State Park, and part of Wayne National Forest lies inside the county.

QuickFacts estimates 32,817 residents for July 2025. It lists 14,665 housing units, 73.9% owner-occupied, with a typical owner-occupied value of $150,700 and median household earnings of $57,106. Workers spend 29.4 minutes getting to their jobs on average, the longest commute among Holmes, Huron and Jefferson counties, and 15.5% of residents are in poverty. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024 and 422 square miles of total area.

faqs.q: How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: $47.00 by the fee page's formula: $39.00 for pages one and two plus $8.00 for the third. A marginal notation adds $4.00 each, so ask the office whether any apply.

faqs.q: Is the Jackson County Recorder open over lunch?
faqs.a: No. The county page says the office closes from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm, and that it is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: What conveyance fee does Jackson County charge?
faqs.a: The Auditor's page lists $4.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price and $0.50 per parcel for transfer. The county has charged $4.00 per thousand since March 24, 1993.

faqs.q: Does paying the Jackson County Recorder by card cost extra?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder's site says debit and credit cards are accepted with a $2.00 service fee. Cash and checks have no added charge.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County Recorder record wills?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder's site says a will is recorded in Probate Court and gives the cost as $46.00. The Recorder files deeds, mortgages and similar land records.
